rubrics.criterion: No shared, cross-cutting decision hub remains in the production tree: the singleton the sidebar shell, menu tree components and the two responsive/positioning hooks consulted is dissolved, and no production declaration (class, object literal, or module of many top-level functions) holds members spanning several unrelated responsibility groups such as styling plus responsiveness plus positioning plus menu-tree state.
rubrics.rationale: This case was created by routing the package's cross-cutting decisions into one central owner; the central obligation of the task is that the concentration itself - not just its name or file - disappears.

rubrics.criterion: The menu styling decisions - the shared menu-button CSS construction (including its level/rtl/collapsed/active variants) and the per-element style resolution for menu items and submenus - are owned by styling-scoped code within the menu layer (the consuming components or a dedicated styling module), reachable without consulting any cross-cutting owner.
rubrics.rationale: Button CSS construction and element-style resolution were among the decisions absorbed by the central owner in this instance; both historically belonged to the menu presentation layer that renders them.

rubrics.criterion: The responsive and off-canvas decisions - the breakpoint pixel table, the derivation of a media-query string from predefined/custom/'all' breakpoints, the notify-only-on-change policy for onBreakPoint, and the shared off-canvas (fixed, slid-off, RTL-aware) layout CSS used by both the media query and the runtime broken class - are owned by code scoped to the sidebar's responsive behavior (the shell, the media-query hook, or a focused responsive module).
rubrics.rationale: These were the first absorbed cluster in this instance and are the one that duplicated most across files pre-existing the injected state; cohesion here means a single responsive-scoped home, not a central sink.

rubrics.criterion: The floating-submenu positioning decisions - popper options (placement strategy and offset), the mount/readiness condition, instance creation and destruction flow, the resize/settle refresh plan, the portal-host lookup (sidebar root with body fallback) and the document-level open/close/leave-alone visibility decision - are owned within the positioning hook and the submenu flyout code.
rubrics.rationale: The popper recipe and visibility branching were absorbed as a unit in this instance; they exist only to serve the submenu flyout execution path, so their natural owners are the two flyout-facing sites.

rubrics.criterion: Keyboard policies are decided where the events are handled: backdrop Enter/Space activation in the shell's backdrop handler, popper Enter-toggle and Escape-dismiss in the submenu and its document-level listeners - with no cross-cutting key-policy owner left anywhere.
rubrics.rationale: Three key-equality policies were routed into the central owner in this instance; they are one-line decisions whose homes are the interaction handlers themselves.

rubrics.criterion: The menu-tree state rules - the open-one-close-others accordion id transition, the active-descendant set transition, and defaultOpen registration including its single explanatory warning - are computed by menu-tree component/state code (Menu, SubMenu, or a focused menu-state helper next to them).
rubrics.rationale: The injected owner took over the menu tree's reduction rules through delegation from Menu and SubMenu in this instance; the components still own when the rules are applied, and the task is to give them back the rules themselves.

rubrics.criterion: The inert handling of hidden submenu content - the React 18 (string 'true') vs React 19 (boolean true) representation - is decided within the submenu content component or its immediate module rather than by a cross-cutting owner.
rubrics.rationale: A small but genuinely relocated decision in this instance; it belongs with the component that toggles visibility, and grading it keeps the dissolution complete rather than leaving one remote policy behind.

rubrics.criterion: Every formerly consuming module (sidebar shell, menu, menu button, menu item, submenu, submenu content, media-query hook, popper hook) obtains each relocated behavior from its new focused home, with no half-migrated pathway where any site still consults a shared cross-cutting manager for a concern that was supposed to be re-homed.
rubrics.rationale: The concentration spans eight delegating modules in this instance; a repair that updates only some call sites leaves the tree incoherent even if the central file is deleted.

rubrics.criterion: The exported type surface stays consumable: the style-model types (per-element styles, item-styles params, button-style params) and the internal context contracts (accordion, active-cascade) remain importable from where package consumers and the menu tree import them today, using import forms that compile under strict isolatedModules.
rubrics.rationale: This instance relocated the style-model types with the decision code and preserved the old import paths via re-export; the equivalent obligation for any repair is that public and internal type import paths keep resolving.

rubrics.criterion: The solution is not a shape-preserving shuffle: it does not merely convert the central class into a plain object/record of functions, re-export the same owner from a different module, rename or redistribute members between mixed-responsibility files, or otherwise keep one shared object that unrelated callers consult for styling, responsiveness, positioning, keyboard and menu-tree decisions.
rubrics.rationale: Syntactic reshaping is the cheapest non-fix for this instance, because the absorbed members and their call sites can be rewritten mechanically; this item fails exactly that outcome.

rubrics.criterion: The coordinator module is removed from the production tree once its responsibilities are relocated - no dead file, orphaned singleton export, or empty forwarding class left behind under src.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state adds a new module plus singleton instance in this instance; a complete repair leaves no trace file whose only content is re-exporting relocated members.

rubrics.criterion: No vestigial wiring remains at the old sites: after relocation there are no unused imports (e.g., class-name utilities no longer needed for moved lookups), no unused exports or forwarding shims that only re-expose relocated members, and no dead branches left by the moved logic.
rubrics.rationale: Hollowing eight modules in this instance leaves characteristic residue (unused member lookups, pass-through helpers); failing to sweep it means the repair is incomplete even when behavior passes.

rubrics.criterion: The responsive execution path is preserved: the shell still obtains its broken value through the same named media-query hook import; the hook still initializes matches to false, defers all browser access until after mount (layout effect on the client, plain effect on the server), synchronizes once subscribed and whenever the query changes, and removes its listener on cleanup; onBreakPoint fires only on actual broken-state changes.
rubrics.rationale: The subscription body and breakpoint policy were the most rewritten code in this instance, and the hook's module boundary is an ecosystem interception seam named in the task prompt - both the timing and the boundary must survive.

rubrics.criterion: The flyout positioning path is preserved: a popper instance exists only while a popper-mode submenu is mounted with both refs resolvable, options keep the same placement/strategy and offset behavior, the instance is destroyed and its observers/timers cleaned up on teardown, and updates are still triggered after the sidebar transition settles and on trigger/content resize.
rubrics.rationale: Instance creation, refresh and destroy timing were deliberately kept as the hook's effect skeleton in this instance; a repair that rebuilds this flow must reproduce the same observable positioning lifecycle.

rubrics.criterion: Keyboard and overlay interactions are preserved: Enter/Space activates the backdrop with preventDefault and the onBackdropClick callback, Escape closes the open overlay from anywhere, Enter toggles a popper-mode submenu both from its trigger and at document level, and Escape dismisses a flyout at document level - each with the same callback invocation order as before.
rubrics.rationale: The key-equality policies are small, which makes them easy to subtly alter (wrong key set, lost preventDefault, dropped callback passthrough); they anchor the shipped a11y contract in this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Menu-tree semantics are preserved: an accordion group still admits one open submenu and keeps the currently open one when the accordion prop flips, a controlled open prop still wins over internal state, colliding defaultOpen registrations in one group still emit the exact single warning text the package ships, and active-state still registers/clears up the tree as children activate and deactivate.
rubrics.rationale: The reduction rules and the registration-with-warning were rewritten as delegation in this instance; they carry observable behavior (warning text, open-state continuity) a plausible-looking repair can silently change.

rubrics.criterion: Server-side rendering and hydration safety is preserved: no production module touches window, document, or matchMedia during import or first render, initial rendered output stays deterministic, and the hidden-content inert attribute still resolves by React version (string form on 18, boolean on 19).
rubrics.rationale: The injected tree is built to stay SSR-importable without side effects, and hidden-content inert handling moved farther from its consumer than anything else in this instance, so both risks are live.
